# Celestia Product Requirements

**Status:** Draft 0.1  
**Owner:** Celestia repository owner  
**Implementation:** Application scaffold only; product capabilities below are not implemented

## Problem

Users interested in Zi Wei Dou Shu need a consistent way to calculate and inspect charts and request interpretations without exposing more personal data than necessary.

## Initial product goals

1. Produce reproducible charts from validated birth inputs.
2. Present the resulting palace and star data clearly.
3. Provide AI-assisted explanations grounded in calculated chart facts.
4. Protect saved charts with authentication and per-user authorization.

## Candidate later capabilities

- Two-chart compatibility analysis.
- Chart sharing with explicit permission and revocation.
- Practitioner consultations and annotations.
- Administrative controls and abuse reporting.
- Authenticated public API with revocable keys.

These capabilities are candidates for subsequent milestones. Their exact priority, data model, and acceptance criteria require product decisions.

## Quality requirements

- Deterministic calculation with regression fixtures.
- Server-side validation and authorization.
- Data minimization for sensitive birth information.
- Accessible navigation and status feedback.
- Observable error handling and documented API contracts.

## Open decisions

- Calculation library and license compatibility.
- Authentication provider and persistence strategy.
- Hosting, budget, and AI service limits.
- Initial design references and release schedule.

## Source boundary

This specification is an independent synthesis of desired capabilities. It does not establish joint authorship with contributors to any reference repository. No third-party source code is included.
# Architecture

**Status:** Application scaffold implemented for Issue #1. The logical components
below remain proposed beyond the minimal homepage.

## Application foundation

The scaffold uses Next.js App Router, React, and strict TypeScript, as requested in
Issue #1. Route components and the root layout live in `src/app`; tests live in
`tests`. Styling uses plain CSS. No application services or persistence exist yet.
Future calculation code must remain independent of route components and AI code.
See [dependencies](dependencies.md) for exact versions and license notes.

`next.config.ts` sets `agentRules: false` so development startup does not create or
rewrite instruction files. This preserves explicit control of `AGENTS.md` for the
planned Issue #3 experiment; no experimental branches have been created.

## Logical components

1. **Chart engine:** Pure functions that transform validated inputs into structured chart data.
2. **Application interface:** Accessible forms, chart visualization, and reading history.
3. **Application API:** Request validation, authentication, authorization, and rate limiting.
4. **Interpretation service:** Converts selected chart facts into constrained AI requests and streams responses.
5. **Persistence:** Encrypted or otherwise appropriately protected private records, with ownership checks.

## Design constraints

- A language model must not be the source of calculated chart positions.
- Sensitive input must be minimized before interpretation requests.
- External integrations must be reviewed for licensing and data handling.
- Data access must be enforced server-side.
- Any proposed technology stack must be confirmed before dependencies are added.

## Verification plan

Establish fixed calculation fixtures, API contract tests, authorization tests, and accessible interaction tests during implementation.

## Open decisions

Database, hosting, authentication provider, calculation engine, and model provider have not been selected for this independent implementation.
# Scaffold dependencies

Issue #1 selects Next.js App Router with React and TypeScript. Versions are pinned
in `package.json`; `package-lock.json` records resolved transitive dependencies.
No source code was imported from another application repository.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| next | 16.4.3 | App Router, development server, production build | MIT |
| react | 19.3.1 | UI components | MIT |
| react-dom | 19.3.1 | React rendering | MIT |
| typescript | 5.9.3 | Static type checking | Apache-2.0 |
| eslint | 9.39.5 | Lint runner | MIT |
| eslint-config-next | 16.4.3 | Next.js, React, and TypeScript lint rules | MIT |
| tsx | 4.23.15 | TypeScript execution for Node's test runner | MIT |
| @types/node | 26.6.6 | Node.js type definitions | MIT |
| @types/react | 19.3.0 | React type definitions | MIT |
| @types/react-dom | 19.3.0 | React DOM type definitions | MIT |

License metadata was checked in the npm registry before integration. MIT and
Apache-2.0 permit this use; retain dependency copyright and license notices when
redistributing third-party material, including any applicable Apache notices.
This repository has not selected its own distribution license. Review obligations
again before distributing a release.

TypeScript 5.9 is within the installed TypeScript lint tooling's supported range;
the registry's current TypeScript 7 release is outside that range. ESLint 9 avoids
the ESLint 10 peer-version gaps documented by Next.js, but npm marks ESLint 9.39.5
as unsupported. This is a tooling maintenance limitation; update once the included
React and accessibility plugins declare compatible peer ranges. See the
[verification record](scaffold-verification.md) for audit findings.

Setup references: [Next.js installation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/installation)
and [Next.js ESLint configuration](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/eslint).
# Issue #1 scaffold verification

Scope: [Issue #1](https://github.com/yikangliu823/Celestia/issues/1).
Baseline commit: `c7e0ce5323f65f4dc0157b748edce60b36be97bf`.
Environment: macOS, Node.js `26.11.0`, npm `11.20.0`.
Branch: `feature/issue-1-app-scaffold`.

## Dependency installation

The first type-check and production build exited 1 with:

```text
tests/home-page.test.tsx(9,64): error TS1501: This regular expression flag is only available when targeting 'es2018' or later.
```

The smoke test used the dotAll regex flag with an ES2017 target. Replacing that
flag with an ES2017-compatible character class fixed both checks. Initial lint
and smoke-test runs already passed. All checks were rerun after the fix and the
Next.js configuration change.

## Runtime checks

Both `npm run dev` and `npm start` were started sequentially on port 3000. HTTP
requests to `/` returned 200. Responses contained the Celestia heading inside the
main landmark, `lang="en"`, and the Celestia document title. No form was present.
Both processes were stopped after verification. These were HTTP checks, not browser
interaction or visual accessibility tests.

The first development start appended a managed block to `AGENTS.md`. The scaffold
now sets `agentRules: false` in `next.config.ts`. The original instruction file was
restored byte-for-byte; repeated startup confirmed it remains unchanged and no
`CLAUDE.md` is created. This removes the observed automatic instruction mutation;
it does not claim full isolation from global or inherited Codex instructions.

## Dependency audit and limitations

`npm audit` exited 1 with 16 moderate findings in the development lint dependency
tree, rooted in minimatch advisory
[GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249).
`npm audit --omit=dev` exited 0 with actual output:

```text
found 0 vulnerabilities
```

The audit suggested breaking downgrades of ESLint and eslint-config-next. Those
were not applied. No transitive major-version overrides were introduced. ESLint
9.39.5 is deprecated but matches the included plugins' declared peer ranges;
these development tooling issues remain maintenance work.

The one automated test covers static homepage rendering only. No coverage
percentage, browser test coverage, chart behavior, or Issue #3 functionality is
claimed. No authentication, database, or AI integration was added.
# Celestia

Celestia is an independent software project exploring deterministic Zi Wei Dou Shu chart generation and AI-assisted chart interpretation.

## Project status

The Issue #1 application scaffold provides a minimal Next.js App Router homepage,
strict TypeScript checking, ESLint, and one automated render smoke test. Birth-input
forms, chart calculation, authentication, persistence, and AI services are not implemented.

## Local development

Use Node.js 22.13 or newer and npm. Verification used Node.js 26.11.0 and npm 11.20.0.
No environment variables or provider credentials are required.

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). Stop the server with Ctrl+C.

## Verification and production

```sh
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm test
npm run build
npm start
```

`typecheck` generates Next.js route types before running TypeScript, including on
a fresh checkout. `lint` treats warnings as failures. `test` uses Node's test runner
with `tsx` to render the homepage and check its application heading inside the main
landmark; it is not a browser or end-to-end test. `start` serves the production build
at [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) and requires a successful build first.

See [scaffold verification](docs/scaffold-verification.md) for recorded results and
[dependencies](docs/dependencies.md) for pinned versions and license notes.

## Repository structure

```text
src/app/
  layout.tsx             Root HTML layout and metadata
  page.tsx               Minimal Celestia homepage
  globals.css            Base responsive styles
tests/
  home-page.test.tsx      Homepage render smoke test
docs/                    Product, architecture, dependency, and verification records
eslint.config.mjs         Next.js and TypeScript lint rules
next.config.ts            Disable automatic agent instruction generation
tsconfig.json            Strict TypeScript configuration
package.json             Scripts and direct dependencies
package-lock.json        Reproducible dependency resolution
```

## Planned capabilities

- Calculate reproducible natal charts using a documented calculation library.
- Display chart data in an accessible interface.
- Explain structured chart data through a server-side AI service.
- Store private charts with authenticated access.
- Explore compatibility analysis and practitioner workflows in later iterations.

## Engineering documents

- [Product requirements](docs/product-requirements.md)
- [Engineering rules](AGENTS.md)
- [Architecture decisions](docs/architecture.md)

## Intellectual property

Celestia is an independent project. External repositories may inform engineering decisions, but their code, assets, text, and documentation must not be copied without an explicit license review. Any subsequently incorporated third-party material must retain the notices required by its license.

## Interpretation notice

Astrological readings are interpretive cultural content, not scientifically validated predictions. They must not be presented as medical, legal, or financial advice.

# Issue #3: birth-input scope and verification

Implemented against the frozen issue requirements supplied for
`yikangliu823/Celestia#3`, using only this checkout and its product and architecture
documents. All test inputs are synthetic. No dependency versions were changed.

## Implemented behavior

- Required, explicitly labeled Gregorian date, local birth time, and birthplace
  time zone fields. Native text inputs allow malformed entries to receive specific
  format guidance rather than silently normalizing them.
- Pure validation rejects missing values, impossible dates (including Gregorian
  leap-year exceptions), malformed times, unknown time zones, bare abbreviations,
  and raw offsets. It trims surrounding whitespace without mutating its input.
- Keyboard-operable native controls, visible focus styles, linked error summary,
  errors associated with their inputs, focus on the first invalid field after
  submission, and a polite status message. Errors update as users correct fields;
  editing clears a previous success message.
- The action is **Check inputs**. Success describes format checks only and states
  that no chart was calculated and daylight-saving validity was not checked.
- Values remain in component memory. The application does not log, transmit, or
  persist them. Error messages do not interpolate entered values. Controls are
  disabled until hydration, require JavaScript, and omit HTML names so native form
  submission cannot serialize birth inputs. Autocomplete is disabled as a browser
  hint; browser extensions and browser-managed recovery are outside app control.

## Assumptions and unresolved requirements

The scaffold dependency is present. The calculation-interface dependency is not:
there is no engine, schema, or contract in this checkout. `BirthInputValues` is a
provisional UI type, not an implementation of that missing interface. Integration
and completeness of “other required chart inputs” cannot be established yet.

Neither source document defines the following choices. They need product and/or
calculation-interface decisions before chart-ready validation can be claimed:

| Gap | Current limited behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Calendar and lunar/leap-month rules | Gregorian dates only; no conversion. |
| Supported birth-year range, future dates, age constraints | Accepts real dates in years 0001–9999, including future dates; this is a format range, not engine support. |
| Time precision and unknown/approximate birth time | Requires exact minute-format HH:MM; no seconds or unknown-time mode. |
| Location meaning: city, coordinates, geocoding, solar-time corrections | Interprets “location/timezone” as the birthplace’s explicitly entered time zone. Does not collect a place name or coordinates. |
| Time-zone source, aliases, historical accuracy | Accepts UTC or slash-separated IANA identifiers recognized by the runtime’s `Intl` database; runtime versions may differ. No canonicalization or device-zone default. |
| Daylight-saving gaps/overlaps and instant conversion | Checks the date, time, and zone individually. Does not reject nonexistent local times or disambiguate repeated ones. |
| Additional chart inputs, including any sex/gender parameter | No unsupported fields or defaults invented. Required fields await the calculation contract. |
| Submission destination and downstream behavior | Local format-check feedback only; no API or calculation call. |

The product requirement for server-side validation remains applicable to a future
API. There is no server input endpoint in this change. Client validation must not
be treated as sufficient validation at a future server boundary. No chart
calculation, authentication, persistence, or AI services were added.

## Verification

Environment: Node.js `v26.11.0`, npm `11.20.0`.

| Command | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm ci` | Exit 0; added 349 packages, audited 350. |
| `npm run typecheck` | Exit 0; route generation and TypeScript passed. |
| `npm run lint` | Exit 0; no warnings or errors. |
| `npm test` | Exit 0; 52 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. |
| `npm run build` | Exit 0; optimized build and static generation of `/` and `/_not-found` succeeded. |
| `git diff --check` | Exit 0. |

No requested verification command failed, so no failure-driven implementation
fixes were required. The initial suite passed 51 tests; after adding the explicit
no-console test, tests, type checking, and lint passed again.

Installation warned that ESLint 9.39.5 is deprecated and that `esbuild` and
`fsevents` install scripts are not covered by `allowScripts`. No script approvals
or npm configuration changes were made. Installation also reported 18 moderate
vulnerabilities. Follow-up `npm audit --json` exited 1 with those 18 findings in
the lint tooling dependency tree, rooted in minimatch advisory
GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249; the report marked fixes unavailable. These remain unresolved
maintenance issues. `npm audit --omit=dev` exited 0 with `found 0 vulnerabilities`.
The dependency manifest and lockfile are unchanged.

The automated suite covers missing/malformed values, leap years, date/time
boundaries, valid and invalid zones, trimming, nonmutation, multiple errors and
correction, non-echoing errors, no console calls during validation, and explicit
DST limitations. Static render tests check labels, required attributes, error
associations, status markup, the pre-hydration guard, and the homepage.

These tests do not execute browser interactions. Keyboard focus movement,
correction/success transitions, screen-reader announcements, and responsive
rendering have not been verified in a browser. There is no claim of end-to-end or
screen-reader test coverage.

Manual browser follow-up: use Tab/Shift+Tab and Enter to submit empty fields;
confirm focus on date and read each linked error; correct with synthetic values
`2000-01-15`, `14:30`, `Asia/Shanghai`; confirm format-only success; edit a value
and verify success clears; check error links, narrow layouts, and JavaScript-off
messaging. Confirm there are no birth values in requests, URLs, browser storage,
or console output during this flow.
